mcqs.learning_point: Use metal reactivity to predict displacement
mcqs.question: In displacement reactions, how is the metal reactivity series used to predict which metal will replace another in a compound?

options.A: A metal lower in the reactivity series can displace a metal higher in the series from its compound.
options.B: A metal higher in the reactivity series can displace a metal lower in the series from its compound.
options.C: Metals can only displace non‑metals, regardless of reactivity.
options.D: Reactivity series is not relevant for predicting displacement reactions.

mcqs.answer: A metal higher in the reactivity series can displace a metal lower in the series from its compound.
mcqs.explanation: Option B is correct because a metal that is higher (more reactive) in the reactivity series can push out a less reactive metal from its compound. Option A reverses the relationship, C is false as metals can also displace other metals, and D ignores the fundamental role of the reactivity series.

mcqs.question: Which of the following reactions is a double displacement (metathesis) reaction?
mcqs.explanation: Option B shows exchange of ions between two aqueous compounds, forming new products – the hallmark of a double displacement reaction. Option A is a single displacement, C is decomposition, and D is a combination reaction.

mcqs.question: When aqueous solutions of lead(II) nitrate and potassium iodide are mixed, a white solid forms. Which statement best explains this observation?

options.A: A gas is evolved due to a redox reaction.
options.B: A precipitate of lead(II) iodide forms because it is insoluble in water.
options.C: The solutions remain clear because all products are soluble.
options.D: A complex ion is formed, keeping the solution clear.

mcqs.answer: A precipitate of lead(II) iodide forms because it is insoluble in water.
mcqs.explanation: Lead(II) iodide (PbI2) is sparingly soluble, so it falls out as a white precipitate. Options A, C, and D do not describe the actual outcome of this ionic exchange.

mcqs.question: A student adds a piece of copper metal to a solution of silver nitrate. Which type of reaction has occurred?

options.B: Single displacement reaction where copper displaces silver

mcqs.answer: Single displacement reaction where copper displaces silver
mcqs.explanation: Copper is higher than silver in the reactivity series, so it replaces silver ions, forming Cu(NO3)2 and solid Ag. This is a single (or simple) displacement reaction. The other options describe different mechanisms.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about metal reactivity is a common misconception?

options.A: A metal higher in the reactivity series can displace a metal lower in the series.
options.B: All metals react with water in the same way.
options.C: Reactivity series helps predict displacement reactions.
options.D: Gold is less reactive than zinc.

mcqs.answer: All metals react with water in the same way.
mcqs.explanation: Option B is false; metals vary widely in their reaction with water—some react vigorously, some not at all. Options A, C, and D are correct statements about reactivity trends.

mcqs.learning_point: Use metal reactivity to predict displacement
mcqs.question: Given the reactivity series Zn > Fe > Cu, which displacement reaction will occur spontaneously?
mcqs.explanation: Zinc is higher than iron in the series, so it can displace iron from iron(II) sulfate. Option A is also feasible (Fe displaces Cu), but only one answer is required; option C matches the given series directly. Options B and D involve a less reactive metal attempting to displace a more reactive one, which does not occur spontaneously.

mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs correctly distinguishes a double displacement reaction from a single displacement reaction?

options.A: NaCl + AgNO3 → NaNO3 + AgCl (double) ; Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl2 + H2 (single)
options.B: CaCO3 → CaO + CO2 (double) ; NaCl + AgNO3 → NaNO3 + AgCl (single)
options.C: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl2 + H2 (double) ; NaCl + AgNO3 → NaNO3 + AgCl (single)
options.D: Fe + CuSO4 → FeSO4 + Cu (double) ; CaCO3 → CaO + CO2 (single)

mcqs.answer: NaCl + AgNO3 → NaNO3 + AgCl (double) ; Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl2 + H2 (single)
mcqs.explanation: Option A correctly labels the ion‑exchange (double displacement) reaction between NaCl and AgNO3, and the metal‑acid (single displacement) reaction of Zn with HCl. The other options misclassify the reaction types.

mcqs.question: Which of the following reactions will result in the formation of a visible precipitate?
mcqs.explanation: Barium sulfate (BaSO4) is insoluble in water, so it precipitates as a solid. Options A and C produce only soluble ions or water, and D explicitly states no reaction, so no precipitate forms.
